title: The Pdelay_Req cease survives a link or portEnabled toggle; only the 5-minute countdown ends it (Milan v1.2 4.2.6.2.5, 802.1AS-2011 10.2.4.11, Figure 11-8)
body:
**Clause.**
- **Milan v1.2 4.2.6.2.5.** A port that receives Pdelay_Resp from more than one clock identity for each of three successive Pdelay_Req shall cease Pdelay_Req transmission. It resumes when the first of these happens: the link state toggles, portEnabled toggles, pttPortEnabled toggles, or 5 minutes pass.
- **IEEE 802.1AS-2011 10.2.4.11.** portEnabled is TRUE only while MAC_Operational is TRUE and the port is administratively enabled, so a link toggle is a portEnabled toggle.
- **Figure 11-8** (MDPdelayReq, as corrected by Cor1 and Cor2), required by 11.2.15.3:
  - `!portEnabled || !pttPortEnabled` enters NOT_ENABLED.
  - `portEnabled && pttPortEnabled` enters INITIAL_SEND_PDELAY_REQ. That state sends a Pdelay_Req at once and sets `lostResponses = 0` and `asCapable = FALSE`.

**Found by source reading** at `55680bff` and `f97c1803`. This has **not yet been exercised on hardware**: no run so far has toggled the link during a cease. A link-toggle scenario is being added to the in-house qualification, and the result will be posted here.
- **No link input.** The engine has no link, MAC_Operational or portEnabled input: `hdl/top/KL_gptp_engine.sv:58-138` has `rst_n` only.
- **Only the countdown clears the cease.** While `S_CEASE` is set, each 1 s beat only counts `S_CEASECNT` down (`hdl/ucode/gen_gptp_ucode.py:1458-1475`, `_tmr_cease_rule`). `prog_leg_resume` (`:1982-1994`) is the only writer that clears `S_CEASE` after the boot init list. Both values live in scratch that survives a warm reset (`:300-321`).
- **So a link toggle never ends the cease.** The port stays silent until the 5-minute countdown expires. The 5-minute exit itself works: on hardware it measured 302.0 s from the last request, and this is the only part observed so far. So a station re-cabled from a multiple-responder segment to a gPTP bridge would go without Pdelay, asCapable and sync for up to 5 minutes.
- **asCapable on link loss.** Inferred from the same source: it falls only after the lost-response count, about 4 s, instead of at once on `!portEnabled`.

**Expected.**
- **The port.** The engine takes `port_enabled_i`, which the parent drives as MAC_Operational AND administratively enabled.
- **Falling edge: NOT_ENABLED.** No Pdelay_Req is sent, asCapable is FALSE, and `S_CEASE` and `S_CEASECNT` are cleared.
- **Rising edge: INITIAL_SEND_PDELAY_REQ.** One Pdelay_Req goes out on the next transmit opportunity, with lostResponses = 0 and asCapable FALSE until 2 to 5 good exchanges (Milan v1.2 4.2.6.2.4).
- **The 5-minute countdown stays as the other exit.**

**Acceptance.**
- **Toggle exit.** Enter the cease with three duplicated responses, then toggle `port_enabled_i`. The first request after the rising edge comes within one pdelayReqInterval, then every interval.
- **Countdown exit.** Without a toggle, the 5-minute exit is unchanged.
- **Link loss.** asCapable falls on the falling edge, and nothing is transmitted while the port is disabled.
- **Mutants.** A planted mutant that keeps `S_CEASE` across the toggle is caught. So is one that ignores the falling edge.
- **Port change.** The engine port is a parent-visible change. It is recorded for the parent adoption: milan-fpga drives it from its effective link.
